title: Compact TPS probe: lightweight tokens-per-second microbenchmark harness for core models
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Goal: build and maintain a compact, reproducible tokens-per-second (TPS) microbenchmark probe that runs cheaply in CI and locally and exercises our core model serving path. This harness should provide fast signal for regression detection (TPS, p95 latencies, and steady-state variance) and be lightweight enough to run on a small GPU (1 GPU equivalent) within minutes.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: TPS measurement across model variants (fp16, int8/quantized), sequence lengths distribution, KV-cache warmup scenarios, prefix caching effects, and a small golden prompt set that represents production mixes. Integrate with existing metrics pipeline and regression alerting.
- Out-of-scope: full sustained throughput/stress tests (we already have longer running stress suites), exhaustive end-to-end customer traffic replay, and multi-region routing tests.

Design summary:
1) Harness shape: single-file CLI + Docker image that runs a fixed waveform of requests: cold-start samples, short prompts (8-64 tokens), medium (128-256), and long tail (512) with configured concurrency sweeps. Default run targets ~3-5M tokens generated across variants and completes in ~6–8 minutes.
2) Metrics collected: aggregate TPS (tokens/sec), p50/p95/p99 latencies per step, per-token latency distribution, steady-state stddev, KV-cache hit effect delta, and token generation cost estimate. Emit metrics to Prometheus pushgateway and a JSON artifact for CI.
3) Regression detection: CI compares the JSON artifact against a rolling baseline stored in S3. We use a two-tier threshold: soft (notify on Slack, annotate PR) and hard (fail CI) based on % TPS drop and p95 increase. Thresholds are configurable per-model and per-quantization profile.
4) Golden prompts and synthetic load: include a curated set of ~15 prompts per model that covers completion, chat-style, and code-generation tails. Provide a synthetic sampler to expand prompt variety by adding noise and token-length scaling.
5) CI integration: run the compact probe as a job on each runtime merge to main and nightly against pinned model artifacts. Artifacts are uploaded to the benchmarking bucket with metadata (commit, runtime build, Docker tag).

Acceptance criteria:
- The harness runs in CI and completes in <10 minutes on our small CI GPU image.
- Outputs standardized JSON with TPS and latency percentiles and pushed metrics visible in the perf dashboard.
- Regression detector triggers Slack annotation for soft violations and fails the PR for hard violations (configurable).
- Documentation (README) with how to run locally, how to add new prompts/models, and how to interpret results.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We bias for speed and signal: the probe is intentionally small to surface large regressions quickly, not to replace long-running stress tests.
- To avoid noise from multi-tenant infra, we recommend using dedicated CI runner or pinned small GPU images; harness has a warmup loop and disk/memory checks to reduce variance.
- We will sample both synthetic and recorded production-like prompts, but recorded traffic will only be used in private branches due to data sensitivity.
- Quantization profile toggles are exposed as CLI flags (e.g., --quant int8-run) to compare kernel selections.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Compact+TPS+Probe+Design
- Initial PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/2541
- Perf dashboard (probe metrics): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Perf/probe-summary

Deployment and rollout plan:
1) Merge core harness and dockerization behind feature flag.
2) Run nightly against core-models (gpt-small, gpt-medium, and our opt-variants) for 1 week to establish baseline.
3) Confident thresholds tuned and then enable on PR-level (soft alerts only) for 1 release.
4) Flip to hard-fail mode for critical models once stable.

Follow-ups and future work:
- Expand to measure multi-stream throughput and batching sensitivity.
- Add automatic delta analysis that correlates TPS regressions with kernel selection/sequence length distribution.
- Add synthetic jitter injector to validate robustness against transient CPU contention.

Customer impact: low (internal developer tooling), but high importance internally for catching regressions early.
